actors.name: Kela systems (OmaKela e-service and back-end processing)

nodes.name: Household with low income wants housing allowance
nodes.description: A household with a small income living in rental, right-of-occupancy or part-ownership housing considers applying for general housing allowance (yleinen asumistuki).

evidence.quote: If you have a small income, you can get general housing allowance
General housing allowance is available for rental, right-of-occupancy and part-ownership housing.

nodes.name: Estimate allowance with online calculator (optional)
nodes.description: The applicant optionally uses Kela's online calculator to get an estimate of the allowance.

evidence.quote: Use our calculator to check how much housing allowance you might get. The result is an estimate.

nodes.name: Agree on who applies for the household
nodes.description: The household members decide which one member applies on behalf of the entire household (housing allowance is granted to the household as a unit).

evidence.quote: One member of the household applies for housing allowance on behalf of the entire household.
Housing allowance is granted to the household as a unit

nodes.name: Roommates in the same household?
nodes.description: The applicant checks whether roommates sharing the home belong to the same household (e.g. joint responsibility for rent under the rental agreement) and therefore must authorise one representative.

evidence.quote: Roommates can be part of the same household or two different households.
Roommates belonging to the same household must authorise one member of their household to apply for housing allowance for the whole household.

nodes.name: Complete power of attorney form AT5e
nodes.description: Roommates in the same household authorise one household member to represent the communal household using form AT 5e, which is submitted with the application.

evidence.quote: Use the form ‘Power of attorney to represent a communal household’ AT5e (PDF) to authorise one household member.

Complete and submit the form Power of attorney to represent a communal household AT 5e (PDF) with your application if you and your roommate(s) belong to the same household and you represent the household.

nodes.name: Landlord on Kela's direct-reporting list?
nodes.description: The applicant checks whether the landlord is among those that send rental agreement information directly to Kela (a private landlord is never on the list).

evidence.quote: Check the list of landlords who send rental agreement information directly to Kela.
You must always send us your rental agreement if you have rented your flat from a private landlord.

nodes.name: Landlord sends rental agreement information to Kela
nodes.description: Listed landlords send rental agreement and rent amount information directly to Kela, so the applicant does not need to send the agreement.

evidence.quote: Kela gets information about rental agreements directly from certain landlords. If your landlord is on the list below, you do not need to send us your rental agreement or details of the amount of your rent.

nodes.name: Attach copy of signed rental agreement
nodes.description: The applicant includes a copy of the signed rental agreement with the application because Kela does not get it directly from the landlord.

evidence.quote: Send Kela a copy of your signed rental agreement with your application if Kela does not get it directly from your landlord.

nodes.name: First application since moving to Finland?
nodes.description: The applicant checks whether they are applying for the first time since moving to Finland and Kela has not yet checked their or a household member's right to Kela benefits.

evidence.quote: if you are applying for housing allowance for the first time since you moved to Finland and Kela has not yet checked if you or another member of your household qualifies for Kela benefits.

nodes.name: Submit notification of moving to Finland
nodes.description: The applicant submits a notification of moving to Finland in OmaKela or on form Y 77e.

evidence.quote: You must submit a notification of moving to Finland in OmaKela or on the form Notification – Moving to Finland or employment in Finland Y 77e (PDF)

nodes.name: Moving to or staying in another country?
nodes.description: The applicant checks whether they have moved to, or are staying in, another country, which must be reported to Kela.

evidence.quote: Tell Kela about your move to or your stay in another country in OmaKela or on the form Moving from Finland or employment abroad Y 38e (PDF).

nodes.name: Report move or stay abroad
nodes.description: The applicant tells Kela about the move to or stay in another country in OmaKela or on form Y 38e.

evidence.quote: Tell Kela about your move to or your stay in another country in OmaKela or on the form Moving from Finland or employment abroad Y 38e (PDF).

nodes.name: Can the applicant use OmaKela?
nodes.description: The applicant chooses the channel: the OmaKela e-service (Finnish/Swedish) or, if OmaKela cannot be used, the paper form AT 1e by post.

evidence.quote: You can apply for general housing allowance either on a form or in the OmaKela e-service.
Do as follows if you cannot use OmaKela:

nodes.name: Submit application and documents in OmaKela
nodes.description: The applicant submits the application and supporting documents (photographed if not digital) in OmaKela; if OmaKela shows a review application (tarkistushakemus) instead of a new application, it can be used and is processed as a new application.

evidence.quote: Submit your application and supporting documents online.
Submit supporting documents in OmaKela. Take photographs of the documents you are sending if they are not in a digital format.
We will process your application as a new application even if you use the review application.

nodes.name: Give consent to Kela messages in OmaKela (optional)
nodes.description: In OmaKela the applicant can consent to Kela sending messages, which speeds up the application process and other contacts.

evidence.quote: In OmaKela, you can also give consent for Kela to send you messages. This will help make your application process and other contacts with Kela quicker.

nodes.name: Fill in, sign and post form AT 1e
nodes.description: The applicant saves the blank AT 1e form, fills it in, prints and signs it, and posts it with supporting documents to Kela (PL 10, 00056 KELA).

evidence.quote: Apply for housing allowance on the form Application – General housing allowance AT 1e (PDF)
Fill in the form and print it out. Remember to sign the form.
Send the form together with any supporting documents to Kela, PL 10, 00056 KELA.

nodes.name: Application reaches Kela
nodes.description: The application (with supporting documents, plus any landlord-supplied rental information) reaches Kela; the month in which it reaches Kela determines how far back the allowance can be paid.

evidence.quote: You can get housing allowance retroactively for up to one month from the month of application. For example, if you wish to get housing allowance from the beginning of January, your application must reach Kela before the end of February.

nodes.name: Supporting documents missing?
nodes.description: Kela checks whether supporting documents are missing from the application.

evidence.quote: If supporting documents are missing from your application, you will get a reminder about that in OmaKela.

nodes.name: Send missing-documents reminder in OmaKela
nodes.description: Kela reminds the applicant in OmaKela that supporting documents are missing.

evidence.quote: If supporting documents are missing from your application, you will get a reminder about that in OmaKela.

nodes.name: Submit missing documents
nodes.description: The applicant submits the supporting documents Kela reminded them about.

evidence.quote: Submit supporting documents in OmaKela.

nodes.name: Retrieve wage and salary data from Incomes Register
nodes.description: Kela gets wage and salary information from the Incomes Register and uses it when processing the application.

evidence.quote: Kela gets wage and salary information from the Incomes Register and uses this information when processing your application.

nodes.name: More information needed from applicant?
nodes.description: Kela assesses whether it needs more information from the applicant to process the application.

evidence.quote: We may ask you for more information if we need it.

nodes.name: Ask applicant for more information
nodes.description: Kela asks the applicant for the additional information it needs.

evidence.quote: We may ask you for more information if we need it.

nodes.name: Provide requested information
nodes.description: The applicant provides the additional information Kela asked for.

evidence.quote: We may ask you for more information if we need it.

nodes.name: Determine household composition
nodes.description: Kela determines which persons belong to the household (persons sharing a home permanently; one household at a time; rules for spouses, roommates, relatives, children, subtenants).

evidence.quote: A household typically includes the persons sharing a home on a permanent basis. You can only be a member of one household at a time.
A person who has moved to Finland can be considered part of a household if Kela considers the person to be permanently resident in Finland.

nodes.name: Student without exception?
nodes.description: Kela checks whether the applicant is a student who, as a rule, cannot get general housing allowance (students usually get the housing supplement for students), or falls under an exception such as living with a child or having suspended studies.

evidence.quote: If you study, you cannot, as a rule, get general housing allowance. The majority of students can get the housing supplement for students to help with their housing costs.
You live with your own child or your partner’s child.

nodes.name: Permanently resident in Finland?
nodes.description: Kela assesses whether the applicant lives in Finland permanently (usually after living in Finland for one year; EU/EEA/Swiss workers and Ukraine war refugees may qualify).

evidence.quote: You will usually be considered to be living in Finland permanently after you have lived in Finland for one year.
You may have the right to general housing allowance if you have fled the war in Ukraine and you live in Finland permanently.

nodes.name: Housing form eligible?
nodes.description: Kela checks that the housing is rental, right-of-occupancy or part-ownership housing.

evidence.quote: General housing allowance is available for rental, right-of-occupancy and part-ownership housing.

nodes.name: Determine household income and assets
nodes.description: Kela determines the total income and assets of the whole household, including an average income where income does not stay the same for 3 months.

evidence.quote: the amount of housing allowance will depend on the total income and assets of the entire household.
Read about the way we calculate an average income for you if your income does not stay the same for 3 months.

nodes.name: Income within municipal income limit?
nodes.description: Kela checks that household income does not exceed the income limit for the municipality.

evidence.quote: You can get housing allowance if your income does not exceed the income limit for your municipality.

nodes.name: Determine recognised housing costs
nodes.description: Kela determines the housing costs that count; only part of the costs are recognised and they are capped by the municipality-specific maximum housing costs.

evidence.quote: Only part of your housing costs are taken into account when calculating your housing allowance.
The amount of housing allowance you can get cannot exceed the municipality-specific maximum limit for recognised housing costs.

nodes.name: Calculate allowance amount
nodes.description: Kela calculates the allowance from the number of adults and children, income and assets, recognised housing costs, municipal maximum housing costs and the basic deductible.

evidence.quote: the number of adults and children in the household
the basic deductible.

nodes.name: Allowance at least EUR 15 per month?
nodes.description: Kela checks whether the calculated allowance reaches the minimum payable amount.

evidence.quote: If your housing allowance is less than EUR 15 per month, it is not paid out.

nodes.name: Determine start date of allowance
nodes.description: Kela sets the allowance to start on the first day of a month, retroactively at most one month from the month of application.

evidence.quote: Housing allowance is always granted as of the first day of the month. For example, if your rental agreement enters into force on 15 March, you will start receiving housing allowance as of 1 April.
Housing allowance is available retroactively for one month.

nodes.name: Decide to grant housing allowance
nodes.description: Kela makes the decision on the application (allowance amount and start month).

evidence.quote: Go to OmaKela to see if Kela has made a decision on your application.

nodes.name: Issue decision notice
nodes.description: Kela issues the decision notice (only in Finnish or Swedish) showing how much the applicant gets and when it is paid.

evidence.quote: The decision notice is only in Finnish or Swedish.
You will also see how much you will get and when your benefit will be paid.

nodes.name: View decision in OmaKela
nodes.description: The applicant checks in OmaKela whether Kela has made a decision, the amount, and the payment date.

evidence.quote: Go to OmaKela to see if Kela has made a decision on your application. You will also see how much you will get and when your benefit will be paid.

nodes.name: Consent to payment to landlord (optional)
nodes.description: The applicant may give consent for the allowance to be paid directly to the landlord's account.

evidence.quote: Kela can pay the housing allowance directly to your landlord’s account if you give your consent.

nodes.name: Choose payee of the allowance
nodes.description: Kela determines whether the allowance goes to the applicant's bank account or the landlord's account (landlord if the applicant consented or rent has been left unpaid two months in a row).

evidence.quote: Kela pays the housing allowance into your bank account or your landlord’s account on the first banking day of the month.
Kela can also pay the housing allowance directly to the landlord if you have left part of or all your rent unpaid for two months in a row.

nodes.name: Contact applicant before paying landlord (unpaid rent)
nodes.description: When rent has been left unpaid for two months in a row, Kela contacts the applicant before paying the allowance to the landlord.

evidence.quote: In situations like that, we will contact you before we pay your housing allowance.

nodes.name: Wait for first banking day of the month
nodes.description: Payment is scheduled for the first banking day of the month, or the next banking day if banks are closed.

evidence.quote: Kela pays the housing allowance into your bank account or your landlord’s account on the first banking day of the month. If the banks are closed on the scheduled payment date, the housing allowance will be paid on the next banking day.

nodes.name: Pay allowance to applicant's bank account
nodes.description: Kela pays the monthly (tax-free) housing allowance into the applicant's bank account.

evidence.quote: Kela pays the housing allowance into your bank account or your landlord’s account on the first banking day of the month.
The housing allowance is tax-free income.

nodes.name: Pay allowance to landlord's account
nodes.description: Kela pays the allowance directly to the landlord's account (with the applicant's consent, or when rent is unpaid for two months in a row).

evidence.quote: Kela can pay the housing allowance directly to your landlord’s account if you give your consent.
Kela can also pay the housing allowance directly to the landlord if you have left part of or all your rent unpaid for two months in a row.

nodes.name: Retroactive month included in payment?
nodes.description: Kela checks whether the allowance is granted retroactively (available for one month).

evidence.quote: Housing allowance is available retroactively for one month.

nodes.name: Credit retroactive allowance
nodes.description: A retroactive allowance generally appears in the bank account within two banking days of payment.

evidence.quote: If you get housing allowance retroactively, the allowance will generally appear in your bank account within two banking days of payment.

nodes.name: Allowance in payment (awaiting changes or review)
nodes.description: The allowance is paid monthly while the household's circumstances stay the same; it is reviewed on reported changes and at least every 12 months, and ends on termination.

evidence.quote: Kela will review your housing allowance at least every 12 months even if your household’s circumstances do not change.
If you get housing allowance, you must notify us if there are changes in your circumstances or the circumstances of your household, such as changes in income, housing costs or something else.

nodes.name: Report the change to Kela?
nodes.description: The applicant decides whether to report a change (gross income up 400 EUR or down 200 EUR per month, move, rent change of 50 EUR or more, member abroad, tenure change, household composition, subtenant, marriage).

evidence.quote: Let us know if your gross income or the gross income of your household
increases by at least EUR 400 per month
decreases by at least EUR 200 per month.

nodes.name: Report change in circumstances
nodes.description: The applicant (only the person who applied for the household) reports the change in OmaKela, or by post if OmaKela cannot be used.

evidence.quote: Changes can only be reported by the person who applied for housing allowance for the household.
You can report changes in the OmaKela e-service. If you cannot use OmaKela, send your application to Kela by post.

nodes.name: Determine effective date of review
nodes.description: Kela sets the date from which the allowance is reviewed (e.g. first day of the month after the change; first full month for rent changes; moving month if the full month's rent is paid).

evidence.quote: Aino, who receives housing allowance, starts in a new job on 1 February. Her new job causes a change in household income. Kela reviews the housing allowance as of 1 March
Kela will review the housing allowance from the beginning of the first full month of the change in housing costs.

nodes.name: Review housing allowance
nodes.description: Kela reviews the allowance (after a reported change as of the effective date, or at the annual review); the amount may change as a result.

evidence.quote: Kela reviews the housing allowance as of 1 June, and the amount of housing allowance may change as a result of the review.
Kela will review your housing allowance at least every 12 months even if your household’s circumstances do not change.

nodes.name: Recover overpaid benefit from applicant
nodes.description: When changes were not reported and benefit was overpaid, Kela recovers the overpaid benefit first from the person who applied for the benefit.

evidence.quote: If you do not report changes to Kela, you may be paid more benefit than you have the right to. In that case, the overpaid benefit will be recovered from you later.
The benefit is recovered first from the person who applied for the benefit.

nodes.name: Recovery from another adult household member needed?
nodes.description: Kela decides whether, if necessary, to also recover the overpayment from another adult household member.

evidence.quote: If necessary, we may also recover the overpayment from another adult member of the household who had reached the age of 18 when the overpayment occurred.

nodes.name: Recover overpayment from another adult household member
nodes.description: Kela recovers the overpayment from another adult member of the household who was 18 or older when the overpayment occurred.

evidence.quote: If necessary, we may also recover the overpayment from another adult member of the household who had reached the age of 18 when the overpayment occurred.

nodes.name: Overpayment recovery concluded
nodes.description: End state: the overpaid benefit has been recovered from the applicant and, where necessary, another adult household member.

evidence.quote: Read more about the recovery of overpayments.
The benefit is recovered first from the person who applied for the benefit.

nodes.name: Notify Kela of absence of 3 months or more
nodes.description: A person living alone lets Kela know they are away from home for more than 3 months.

evidence.quote: If you live alone, let us know if you are away from your home for more than 3 months. Your right to housing allowance ends if you are away from your home for 3 months or more.

nodes.name: Request that allowance be stopped
nodes.description: An applicant who no longer needs the allowance notifies Kela in OmaKela (Ilmoita muutoksista, or a message) or on form AT 6e.

evidence.quote: If you no longer need housing allowance, let us know that you want your housing allowance stopped. Submit a notification in OmaKela e-service (under Ilmoita muutoksista) or send a message in OmaKela (under Lähetä ja lue viestejä).

nodes.name: End right to housing allowance
nodes.description: Kela ends the allowance when the applicant asks for it to be stopped or when the person living alone has been away 3 months or more.

evidence.quote: Your right to housing allowance ends if you are away from your home for 3 months or more.
let us know that you want your housing allowance stopped.

nodes.name: Housing allowance ended
nodes.description: End state: the right to housing allowance has ended.

evidence.quote: Your right to housing allowance ends if you are away from your home for 3 months or more.

nodes.name: Annual review falls due
nodes.description: Kela reviews the allowance at least every 12 months even if circumstances do not change; the next review date is visible in OmaKela.

evidence.quote: Kela will review your housing allowance at least every 12 months even if your household’s circumstances do not change. You can see the date for your next annual review in OmaKela e-service.

nodes.name: Send annual review instructions in OmaKela
nodes.description: About two months before the scheduled review Kela sends instructions about the annual review as a message in OmaKela.

evidence.quote: We will send you instructions about the annual review of your housing allowance about two months before the review is scheduled to take place. You will receive the message in OmaKela.

nodes.name: Submit annual review application
nodes.description: The applicant sends the information needed for the annual review on the application for general housing allowance, in OmaKela or by post.

evidence.quote: Send us the information needed for the annual review on the application for general housing allowance.

nodes.name: Annual review application submitted in time?
nodes.description: Kela checks whether the applicant submitted the review application in time.

evidence.quote: If you do not submit the application in time for the review, we will have to stop the payment of your housing allowance.

nodes.name: Stop payment of housing allowance
nodes.description: Kela stops the payment because the annual review application was not submitted in time.

evidence.quote: If you do not submit the application in time for the review, we will have to stop the payment of your housing allowance.

nodes.name: Payment stopped after missed annual review
nodes.description: End state: payment of the housing allowance has been stopped because the annual review application was not submitted in time.

evidence.quote: If you do not submit the application in time for the review, we will have to stop the payment of your housing allowance.

nodes.name: No allowance paid
nodes.description: End state: no general housing allowance is paid (not eligible, e.g. student without exception, not permanently resident, income above limit, or allowance under EUR 15 per month).

evidence.quote: If you study, you cannot, as a rule, get general housing allowance.
If your housing allowance is less than EUR 15 per month, it is not paid out.
You can get housing allowance if your income does not exceed the income limit for your municipality.

edges.condition: roommates in the same household and one represents it
landlord is on the list (applicant continues preparing the application)
landlord not on the list (always the case for a private landlord)
landlord supplies rental information directly to Kela
first application since moving to Finland and not yet checked by Kela
moved to or staying in another country
not a student, or an exception applies
allowance EUR 15 per month or more
optional: applicant consents to payment to landlord
applicant has consented to payment to landlord
rent left unpaid for two months in a row
start of next month: entitlement continues
reportable change in the household's circumstances occurs
living alone and away from home for 3 months or more
applicant no longer needs housing allowance
annual review due (at least every 12 months)
change is not reported and benefit is overpaid
review: data gathered again and allowance recalculated
recovery from the applicant is not enough and it is necessary
